title: 6 open-source Android apps I’d use even if they weren’t free
summary: Some of these aren't even on the Play Store.
content: The beauty of Android is the huge ecosystem of awesome open-source apps available for the platform. There is an entire app store called F-Droid that exclusively features free and open-source apps. Some of these apps are so good that I would pay for them if they weren’t free. I’m sharing a few here.

title: Amazon Kids Tablet 11 is 39% off, its lowest price yet
summary: Amazon Kids Tablet 11 is $130 off, matching its lowest tracked price
content: Letting a child use your tablet or phone means keeping an eye on your files, your accounts, and whatever ends up on the screen. A dedicated device takes that off your plate, and the Amazon Kids Tablet 11 now costs $199.99 on Amazon, down from $329.99.

title: 3 award-winning movies to watch on Netflix this weekend (November 27-29)
summary: Finish your month with these showstoppers.
content: The long weekend gives you a chance to catch up on a few movies you may have been meaning to watch, including those recognized by major award shows during their run. For this week’s award-winning Netflix list, I’ve picked a documentary, a dark comedy, and a drama.

title: Can a music CD really still work with a hole drilled in it? I put the old claim to the test
summary: A 1994 factory CD, a 1.5mm drill bit and a backyard experiment uncover why some players ignore physical damage.
content: Music CDs were a revelation when I was growing up. My first experience of recorded music at home was in the form of vinyl records and audio cassettes. Muffled, warbling noises that sort-of sounded like music. The first time I heard a CD in the '90s, it was like someone had taken the cotton wool out of my ears.

title: DREO's quiet space heater is at its lowest price in 90 days for $33.46
summary: 34dB, a 12-hour timer, and 1°F thermostat control. It's the lowest price in 90 days.
content: The DREO Space Heater just hit its lowest price in 90 days at $33.36 on Amazon, and if your bedroom or office feels like a walk-in freezer, this fix won't cost you a night's sleep.

title: How to make a Linux rescue USB with Ventoy that boots any ISO
summary: Computers rarely ask whether it is a convenient time to ruin your day, but this might just save you!
content: Troubleshooting a Linux system that refuses to boot can be particularly frustrating when the tools you need to diagnose the problem are inaccessible. You might need to inspect the bootloader, recover files from a damaged partition, or determine whether a failing SSD is responsible. Preparing the appropriate recovery media when your computer is already out of commission adds another layer of inconvenience.

title: I let Claude Code run my Docker home server, and it does a better job than I ever did
summary: It reads the docs, writes the config and fixes what breaks.
content: I used to launch all my own Docker servers and containers myself. I learned a lot about self-hosting that way. But, these days, I just let Claude Code configure my Docker servers . Not only that, I have Claude Code configure my Docker containers , too.

title: Linux Mint 27 beta is here, but there’s a catch for dual-boot users
summary: Laptop users get easier hibernation controls, although the beta isn't quite ready for everyday computing.
content: Linux Mint has proven popular with desktop Linux users who want a familiar environment without a lot of tweaking. Now, Linux Mint 27 Adrien has reached beta, bringing back hibernation and a number of other changes worth digging into.

title: Make these 5 changes before charging your Pixel Watch overnight
summary: Optimize your Pixel Watch charging conditions by making these changes.
content: Charging your Pixel Watch overnight? Depending on your setup and Pixel Watch model, there are a few steps you can take to improve battery health and the overall charging experience. These changes include settings within your smartwatch, as well as other environmental factors to keep in mind.

title: MSI Pro MP161E6T review: A great choice, as long as you don't need red
summary: The MSI Pro MP161E6T is another solid portable monitor option, especially with its versatile design.
content: There's an overwhelming number of portable markets on the market, making it difficult to decide which best suits your needs — especially given how companies tend to name monitors. The MSI Pro MP161E6T tries to cut through the noise with its practical design and touch-enabled display, but whether this $130 portable monitor is the one for you will depend on your needs. At the very least, the MP161E6T is a worthy successor to the less compelling MSI Pro MP165E6 my colleague reviewed .

title: My wife installed an antivirus app to stop creepy ads, but she didn't need it
summary: Your phone is probably safer than you think. Your data, maybe less so.
content: Antivirus software used to be one of the most important pieces of software you could run on an old Windows PC, so many people reasonably carried this habit over to their phones. Even today, plenty of Android users firmly believe an antivirus app is essential. Just look at the download counts of some of these apps on the Play Store.

title: 3 excellent Netflix documentaries to binge-watch this weekend (November 27-29)
summary: Wrestling, Hollywood, and true crime are the subjects of documentaries to check out.
content: It's a great time to love documentaries, especially if you have Netflix in the U.S. There are several documentaries in the top 10, including Primetime Preacher$, which was one of our picks in last week's article . Primetime Preacher$ brings audiences into the televangelism boom of the 1980s, when greed and scandal brought down one of the movement’s most prominent speakers.

title: I turned my old Samsung into an offline iPod, and I'm not paying for Spotify anymore
summary: Cut down your streaming costs and enjoy the music that you already own.
content: Subscription services have burrowed their way into just about every facet of our lives, including our music-listening habits. There is no denying that music streaming apps are convenient, but they are also heavily algorithmic, cost you a decent chunk of money every month, and are a privacy nightmare. Paying for one makes even less sense if you have a physical library of music that you already own.

summary: Get the Western Digital 8TB Elements Desktop External Hard Drive on Amazon for 28% off and add space for backups and archives.
content: Photo archives, video projects, and full-system backups add up fast, and a laptop's internal drive rarely keeps pace. The Western Digital 8TB Elements Desktop External Hard Drive gives you 8TB of space to keep it all in one place, right on your desk. At the time of writing, it's 28% off on Amazon as part of a Black Friday deal.

title: Save 51% on Sony SS-CS8M2 Center Channel Speaker
summary: Sony's SS-CS8M2 center channel speaker is 51% off on Amazon, with three drivers to keep movie dialogue clear in your home theater.
content: Dialogue can get buried under explosions and swelling music in a loud action scene, which is where a dedicated center channel speaker comes in. Sony's SS-CS8M2 center channel speaker is 51% off on Amazon as part of its Black Friday sale as of this writing, and it's worth a look if you're building or expanding a home theater.

summary: Fix weak Wi-Fi in far-off rooms with 57% off the TP-Link AC750 WiFi Range Extender (RE220) in an Amazon Black Friday deal.
content: There's nothing more frustrating than a dead zone in your own home, especially when you just want to stream a movie in the bedroom. Far-off bedrooms, home offices, and basements are common trouble spots, since your router's signal has to get through walls to reach them. The TP-Link AC750 WiFi Range Extender (RE220) can help extend your signal, and it's 57% off in an Amazon Black Friday deal as of this writing.

title: The ThinkPad T480 had a legendary run, but there is a better budget ThinkPad now
summary: The internet's favorite budget ThinkPad has a worthy successor!
content: For years, whenever someone asked for a recommendation for an inexpensive laptop to run Linux, the Lenovo ThinkPad T480 was one of the easiest recommendations to make. It had a quad-core processor, upgradeable RAM, a removable battery, an excellent keyboard, and a seemingly endless supply of replacement parts. As businesses retired their fleets of these laptops, they became remarkably affordable on the secondhand market.

title: The WiiM Mini Wi-Fi music streamer is at an all-time low for $84.15
summary: It's the lowest price ever, and it adds Wi-Fi streaming to your existing stereo.
content: The WiiM Mini is the cheapest way to give your existing receiver, amplifier, or powered speakers a wireless brain, and it's currently $84.15 on Amazon, down from $99.

title: 5 things you never knew were possible with Home Assistant
summary: There's no place like Home Assistant.
content: Home Assistant is absolutely packed with features, and more get added all the time. Even if you're a seasoned Home Assistant user, there may be features that you've completely missed.

title: This FOSS gym tracker keeps my workout data private, and I can even self-host it
summary: I spent years not tracking my workouts because I didn't like what's on the Play Store.
content: I've been going to the gym four times a week for almost six years now. I'm not exactly a gym rat, but it's one of the few things that regularly gets me out of the house, which is especially important since I work from home.

title: UGREEN's all-flash NAS is at its lowest price yet for just $799.99
summary: It's an all-time-low price on Amazon, and it's designed for video editing.
content: If you edit video or work with large files daily, scattered drives and slow network transfers are a daily tax on your time. UGREEN's DXP480T Plus all-flash NAS removes that tax, and right now it's at its lowest tracked price on Amazon. You pay $799.99 and save $200 off the $999.99 full price on a unit that's built specifically for creators who need speed.

title: This open-source tool gives Windows-only USB accessories a second chance on Linux
summary: Stop wrestling with Wireshark: usb-rea builds Linux drivers for Windows-only USB gear automatically.
content: Linux users have long suffered at the hands of USB accessories that work perfectly fine but lose their configuration features when not in Windows. A new open-source project called usb-rea wants to change that by analyzing USB traffic and outputting Python drivers for otherwise unsupported hardware.

title: I used a Raspberry Pi to bring AirPlay to a 15-year-old surround sound system
summary: Pi fidelity.
content: I've had my surround sound system for more than 15 years and it's lasted through three different TVs. It's certainly not audiophile equipment, but it offers far better sound than the smart speakers in my living room.

summary: Cook up something special this weekend.
content: You can put an ESP32 microcontroller to use all around your home, and that includes the kitchen. Most of us spend a lot of time in there cooking, eating, and hanging out, so why not make the space a little more functional with a weekend project or two.

title: 6 useful laundry room fixes you can 3D print this weekend (Nov 27-29)
summary: Get a helping hand.
content: I love using my 3D printer to fix shortcomings with my home and the appliances therein. Laundry is a chore that nobody enjoys, but everyone has to do, and so making such a tedious job a little easier feels truly within the spirit of the 3D printing hobby.

title: Adventure for less with $100 off the Velotric Discover 3 during Black Friday
summary: This article sponsored by Velotric
content: E-bikes have become an incredibly popular mode of transportation recently. They have all the components of a standard bicycle, except for an integrated motor with a rechargeable battery. The motor provides a little bit of extra oomph (power) to help navigate the toughest terrain or maintain a steadier pace.

title: A Xen bug lets malware escape Qubes OS virtual machines
summary: The flaw affects every supported version of Intel PC
content: Qubes OS uses virtual machines to keep malware from spreading to the rest of your system; it should work so that malware affecting the VM can't break past it and infect your PC.

title: Your Pi-hole might be ignoring all the IPv6 devices on your network, so do a quick sanity check now
summary: Your Pi-hole isn't blocking everything? Check this IPv6 setting first
content: Pi-hole is pretty much all benefits with very few cons. Set it up once, point your network at it, and enjoy fewer ads and unwanted connections without installing software on every device. That's the dream, anyway...
